Join planned observations to saved measurements and select model rows

lexdiv_study_table.Rd

Preserve planned observations, submitted documents and measurement identities in an ordinary research table. Select one response specification with a separate exclusion audit for an existing modelling package. These functions do not fit or choose models, impute missing observations, or recalculate submitted results.

Usage

lexdiv_study_table(planned, submissions, results, plan, condition_id,
                  reporting = NULL, max_rows = 1e6)
lexdiv_study_model_data(study, condition_id, request_id,
                       required = c("writer_id", "task", "occasion"))

Arguments

planned

Data frame with unique nonblank character observation_id, writer_id, task and occasion. Writer/task labels may be character or factors and may be missing. Extra atomic columns, including dates and factors, are retained. Supply actual planned rows; no Cartesian design is inferred. Column names must not collide with result/output fields.

submissions

Data frame with exactly observation_id, document_id and input_characters. IDs are unique nonblank character strings. Each submitted document belongs to one known observation, with at most one document per observation. Character counts are nonnegative whole numbers or NA when unknown.

results

Complete, unchanged result of lexdiv_metrics_batch(documents, plan = plan), including exactly one row for each submitted document and requested specification.

plan

The explicit lexdiv_plan used for results.

condition_id

One nonblank character label for the selected analysis condition. It is a caller declaration, not proof of preprocessing equivalence.

reporting

Optional data frame with exactly document_id, request_id, reporting_status and reporting_reason, covering every submitted document/request pair. Status is "report" or "withhold"; each decision needs a nonblank reason. NULL leaves all rows "not_screened", so none enter model data yet.

max_rows

Positive whole-number limit on planned observations times requested specifications, checked before constructing the table.

study

The complete study table, optionally with multiple explicitly labelled conditions.

request_id

One request in the saved plan. A model selection must contain one method, specification and plan identity and one row per observation.

required

Unique existing metadata column names required for model rows. Missing, blank or non-finite values exclude the row and remain in the audit.

Details

Unsubmitted observations, empty submitted texts, no selected tokens, unavailable scores, reporting decisions and missing metadata remain distinct. Missing values are never converted to zero. The table follows planned-row order, then plan request order. Empty tokens are passed to the public plan executor only to validate the plan and obtain request metadata; submitted values are not recomputed.

Model rows require submitted, computable, explicitly reportable values and complete required metadata. The output is not evidence of an ignorable missing data mechanism, model identifiability or a causal interpretation. Select and justify a model using the research design. Keep original texts, preprocessing inputs, plan, reporting decisions and the complete table in the study record.

Introduced as public interfaces in 0.4.0.9006 with the computations and table layout of the previous installed example. Sourcing examples/study-table.R still defines study_long_table() and study_model_data() with the same arguments and return values. See repeated observations guide.

Value

lexdiv_study_table() returns a plain data frame with planned metadata, measurement fields and condition_id, submission_status, input_status, input_characters, computation_status, reporting_status and reporting_reason.

lexdiv_study_model_data() returns a list with data, the selected ordinary data frame whose row names are observation IDs, and audit, one row per selected-condition/request observation. Audit columns retain IDs, not_submitted, not_computable, not_reportable, missing_metadata and included; several exclusion reasons may coexist.

Examples

plan <- lexdiv_plan(presets = character(), specs = list(
  lexdiv_spec("ttr_v_over_n_v1", request_id = "ttr")))
planned <- data.frame(observation_id = c("o1", "o2"),
  writer_id = c("001", "002"), task = "essay", occasion = 1)
submissions <- data.frame(observation_id = "o1", document_id = "d1",
  input_characters = 5)
results <- lexdiv_metrics_batch(list(d1 = c("a", "b", "a")), plan = plan)
reporting <- data.frame(document_id = "d1", request_id = "ttr",
  reporting_status = "report", reporting_reason = "Planned specification")
study <- lexdiv_study_table(planned, submissions, results, plan,
  "surface-all", reporting)
selected <- lexdiv_study_model_data(study, "surface-all", "ttr")
selected$audit
#>   observation_id document_id condition_id request_id not_submitted
#> 1             o1          d1  surface-all        ttr         FALSE
#> 2             o2        <NA>  surface-all        ttr          TRUE
#>   not_computable not_reportable missing_metadata included
#> 1          FALSE          FALSE                      TRUE
#> 2           TRUE           TRUE                     FALSE
